```{r}
#| label: path-session-setup
#| include: false

course_root <- getwd()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = NA)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))

default_output_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  default_output_hook(gsub(course_root, "C407", x, fixed = TRUE), options)
})

mpg_hp_plot <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(mpg, hp))
```

## The working directory is R’s starting point

The working directory is the folder R is currently using.

::: {.fragment}
It is the default location R uses when it reads or writes a file.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Check it directly in the Console:

```{r}
getwd()
```

Positron also displays the current directory in the Console action bar.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
- Positron workspaces and R project files: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## Opening C407 sets the starting point

In Positron, choose **File → Open Folder…** and select the **C407** folder.

The active R Console then uses C407 as its working directory.

```{r}
getwd()
```

### Does the result end with `C407`?

::: {.key-point}
Open the C407 folder itself—not `C407.Rproj`.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Positron workspaces and R project files: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## R first looks in the working directory

Load the tidyverse:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

This command looks for `bca262.rds` directly inside C407:

```{r}
bca <- read_rds("bca262.rds")
```

::: {.fragment}
It fails because the file is inside the **Data** subfolder.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
:::

## A relative path starts from C407

Tell R how to travel from the working directory to the file:

```{r}
bca <- read_rds("Data/bca262.rds")
dim(bca)
```

::: {.fragment}
::: {.path-line}
`C407` → `Data` → `bca262.rds`
:::

Use the Explorer to confirm that `bca262.rds` is inside the `Data` folder.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
- Positron interface overview: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio.html
:::

## Relative paths remain portable

- Use `/` between folders: `Data/bca262.rds`.

::: {.fragment}
- Relative paths are shorter than full absolute paths.
- They keep working when the entire C407 folder moves to a new location.

::: {.key-point}
Keep the internal folder structure unchanged, and the same relative paths work on another computer.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
:::

## Create a plot in the R session

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```r
mpg_hp_plot <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(mpg, hp))

mpg_hp_plot
```

The plot appears in Positron’s **Plots** pane.
:::

::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-alt: "Scatterplot showing vehicle horsepower against miles per gallon."

mpg_hp_plot
```
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
:::

## The path controls where the plot is saved

Save in the working directory:

```r
ggsave(
  "mpg_hp.png",
  width = 8, height = 4.5
)
```

::: {.fragment}
Save in the Temp subfolder:
:::

::: {.fragment}
```r
ggsave(
  "Temp/mpg_hp.png",
  width = 8, height = 4.5
)
```

Use the Explorer to confirm that the two files are in different folders.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
:::

Restart the R interpreter with `Ctrl/Command + Shift + 0` and open the C407 folder as the workspace.

Load `2021_census_pumf_ind.rds` from the `Data` subfolder and assign it to `pumf`:

```r
pumf <- read_rds(____________________)
```

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
- Positron keyboard shortcuts: https://positron.posit.co/keyboard-shortcuts.html
:::

## The path begins at C407

```{r}
pumf <- read_rds("Data/2021_census_pumf_ind.rds")
dim(pumf)
```

::: {.path-line}
`C407` → `Data` → `2021_census_pumf_ind.rds`
:::

The path does not include folders above C407, so it remains portable.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
:::

## The PUMF contains individual-level census data

The course file contains **980,868 anonymized records** from the 2021 Census Individuals File.

- It represents a **2.7% sample** of the Canadian population.
- It contains social, demographic, and economic characteristics.
- Detailed geography is restricted to protect confidentiality.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source and record count: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
- Statistics Canada, Individuals File, 2021 Census PUMF: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/98M0001X2021001
:::

## Browse before you analyse

Open the first six rows in Positron’s Data Explorer:

```r
pumf |>
  head() |>
  View()
```

Look for variables that describe:

- age and gender;
- education and employment;
- income and housing; and
- province or census metropolitan area.

::: {.key-point}
Inspecting names and values is the first step toward choosing variables responsibly.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/04_Working_Directory_Relative_Path.Rmd`.
- Statistics Canada, Individuals File, 2021 Census PUMF: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/98M0001X2021001
- Positron Data Explorer: https://positron.posit.co/data-explorer.html
:::

## A compact preview shows names and values

::: {.scroll-output}
```{r}
pumf |>
  select(1:8) |>
  head()
```
:::

Use this preview to connect the variable names to the categories you see in the Data Explorer.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course data: `Data/2021_census_pumf_ind.rds`.
:::
